sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Anopam Chouhan, Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Viraj Godha, Panel Lawyer for the non-applicant/St  None for the prosecutrix, though served.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second application filed u/S 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.214/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Kanwan, District Dhar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 376, 376(2)(n),
376(d), 342, 323 and 34 of IPC alongwith 5(l)6 of the POCSO Act.
2. His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 14.11.2024 passed in MCRC No.45379/2024.

3. Prosecution story, in brief is that on 30.08.2023, prosecutrix alongwith his father went to her relative's house on the occasion of rakhi, where two unknown persons came at the house with their faces covered with cloth and gave money to her father and aunt and forcibly took the prosecutrix to the house of one NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:629 2 MCRC-54973-2024 Rakesh where they committed rape upon her repeatedly, due to which she got pregnant.
Later on, she ran away to her grandparents house and lodged the report against the accused persons.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant/accused has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that after dismissal of his earlier Jeevan@ Krishna vs State Of Mp on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34767408/
1 bail application, prosecutrix (PW-1), her grandfather (PW-2) and grandmother (PW-3) have been examined before the Trial Court but they have not supported the case of prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case of prosecution is also not supported by DNA report in respect of the applicant.
Applicant is in custody since 10.06.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that present applicant/accused be released on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has objected the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed t hat applicant- Jeevan @ Krishna shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court, for his appearance before the concerned Court regularly on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr. P. C/480(3) of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:629 3 MCRC-54973-2024 BNSS.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of tri al but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
9. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
